faq.q: Do I need a fishing license to fish from a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, if you are 16 or older. Spanish law requires a recreational fishing license for all sea fishing, including from a charter boat. The license is issued by the Junta de Andalucía and must be carried with you (digital copy accepted). Children under 16 do not need a license when accompanied by a licensed adult.

faq.q: How do I get a fishing license for Marbella boat rental?
faq.a: Apply online through the Junta de Andalucía's website. You'll need your NIE or passport, and a payment method. The license costs around €10–€15 and is valid for one year. Processing is usually instant – you'll receive a digital copy by email. Print it or save it on your phone.

faq.q: Can I fish from any of your boats without a license?
faq.a: No. All anglers aged 16 and over must have a valid fishing license. Our skippers will ask to see it before departure. If you don't have one, we can help you apply online before your trip – but it's your responsibility to have it.

faq.q: What fishing gear is included on your charters?
faq.a: We provide rods, reels, tackle, and bait on all our boats – at no extra cost. Just bring your fishing license and sunscreen. Our skippers know the best spots for bream, sea bass, and bonito – and will happily help you set up.

faq.q: Are there size and bag limits for fish caught in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes. The Junta de Andalucía sets minimum sizes and daily bag limits for each species. For example, sea bass must be at least 36cm, and you can keep up to 5 per day. Our skippers will inform you of current limits – and we encourage catch-and-release for undersized fish.

faq.q: Is spearfishing allowed on your boat rentals?
faq.a: No. Spearfishing is not permitted on any of our charters. It requires a separate license and is strictly regulated. Our boats are for rod-and-line fishing only – which is safer and more relaxing for everyone on board.

faq.q: What happens if I forget my fishing license?
faq.a: You won't be able to fish. Our skippers are required to check licenses before departure. If you forget it, you can still enjoy the cruise, but no fishing lines will be deployed. We recommend saving your digital license on your phone before you arrive.

faq.q: Do you offer fishing-specific boat rentals?
faq.a: Yes. All our boats are available for fishing – from the [Astondoa 40](/boats/astondoa-40/) to the [Mangusta 80](/boats/mangusta-80/). For serious anglers, we recommend the [Azimut 39](/boats/azimut-39/) for its open cockpit. Just let us know you're fishing when booking.

data.body_html:
Planning a fishing trip from Marbella in 2035? The rules are straightforward, but you need to get them right. In this guide, we cover who needs a fishing license, how to get one, what's included on our charters, and the key regulations you'll face. We'll also point you to the best boats for fishing – all departing from Puerto Banús.

Who needs a fishing license in Marbella?

In 2035, Spanish law requires a recreational sea fishing license for anyone aged 16 or older. This applies whether you're fishing from the shore, a kayak, or a chartered boat. Children under 16 can fish without a license, but only when accompanied by an adult with a valid license. The license is issued by the Junta de Andalucía and is valid for all coastal waters in the region.

How to get your fishing license – step by step

The good news: it's easy and cheap. Apply online via the Junta de Andalucía's official portal. You'll need your passport or NIE, and a credit/debit card. The fee is around €10–€15, and you'll receive your digital license instantly by email. Since 2030, paper licenses are no longer accepted – you must show the digital version on your phone or a printed copy.

If you're not comfortable applying online, our team can help you before you board. Just arrive 30 minutes early and we'll walk you through the process. But note: we cannot issue the license – it's a government service.

Fishing from our Marbella boat rental – what's included

Every boat charter with us includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. For fishing, we also provide rods, reels, tackle, and bait – at no extra cost. The skipper will take you to the best fishing spots around Marbella, from the rocky bottoms near Cala del Faro to the deeper waters off Cabopino.

Our most popular fishing boats are the [Astondoa 40](/boats/astondoa-40/) (12.5m, 9 pax) and the [Azimut 39](/boats/azimut-39/) (12.5m, 11 pax), both departing from Puerto Banús. For a more exclusive experience, the [Mangusta 80](/boats/mangusta-80/) (24m, 12 pax) offers a flybridge with panoramic views – perfect for spotting tuna schools.

Fishing regulations you must know in 2035

Beyond the license, there are strict rules on what you can catch and keep. The Junta de Andalucía sets minimum sizes and daily bag limits. For example: sea bass minimum 36cm, bream 23cm, and bonito 25cm. Daily bag limits vary – typically 5–10 fish per species per angler. Our skippers know the current limits and will advise you on the spot.

Spearfishing is strictly prohibited on our charters. Also, you cannot sell any fish caught – it's for personal consumption only. And remember: catch-and-release is encouraged for undersized fish, and our skippers are happy to help you handle them safely.

What about fishing from a private boat vs. a charter?

If you rent a boat without a skipper (bareboat), you still need the same fishing license. The license is tied to the angler, not the boat. However, we always recommend a skippered charter – not only for safety but because our skippers know the local waters and fishing grounds intimately. They'll put you on the fish.

Best seasons for fishing in Marbella

Fishing is good year-round, but the species change with the seasons. In spring (March–May), sea bass and bream are active near the shore. Summer (June–August) brings bonito and small tuna. Autumn (September–November) is prime time for larger tuna and amberjack. Winter (December–February) is quieter but still productive for bream and hake.

Water temperatures range from 15°C in winter to 24°C in summer – so plan your clothing accordingly. And always book your charter in advance, especially in July and August when boats sell out.

Our top boats for fishing trips

All our boats are fishing-friendly, but some are better suited than others. For small groups, the [Bandido](/boats/bandido/) (11.5m, 8 pax) is a sporty option with a large cockpit. For families, the [Lagoon 380](/boats/lagoon-380/) (11.6m, 10 pax) is a stable catamaran – great for kids. And for a luxury day out, the [Ferretti 94](/boats/ferretti-94/) (29m, 12 pax) offers unparalleled comfort.
